── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 32, 24, 27, 37 mi
This week: 53 mi over 6 runs. Planned 38 mi, ran 53 mi.
Body: "Calves tight on Sunday night, otherwise great."
Feeling: "Like I've turned a corner."
Asks: "I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: You are fitter than the plan assumed, but going from 37 to 53 miles in one week is how injuries start. …
Answers: (1) Not at this level, and not by adding miles to every run. The fitness is real. (2) The problem is that heart and lungs adapt faster than calves, tendons and bones. A 43% jump in one week is where overuse injuries start. (3) What you can keep up is steady training at the planned distances. Treat each one as the most you run that day.
Next week:
Mon: rest. A true rest day with no extra run, so the 20-miler can sink in and the calves…
Tue: easy, 7 mi, heart rate under 145, flat route, stop at 7 mi. Gets your rhythm back…
Wed: quality, 8 mi, with 2 mi easy, 4 mi continuous at 8:30–8:35/mi, then 2 mi easy; one…
Thu: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145, stop at 5 mi. Keeps the day after the session…
Fri: rest. A full day off before the weekend.
Sat: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145, with 4 x 20 s relaxed strides at the end. Keeps…
Sun: long, 14 mi, heart rate under 145 for the first 10 mi and under 150 to the end…
